title: Hypothalamic oxytocin neuron activation rescues cardiac metabolism through cardiac cholinergic signaling in type 2 diabetes
text:
Diabetic cardiovascular autonomic neuropathy is among the most common yet least understood complications
of type 2 diabetes (T2D) despite significant negative impact on survival and quality of life. A goal of this project
is to identify the effects of T2D on brainstem-originating neuronal communication to the heart in a model of high
fat diet and streptozotocin-induced T2D in rats. Our studies will also test the innovative hypothesis that timed
activation of a small population of hypothalamic paraventricular neurons will slow the development of, or reverse,
the deleterious autonomic and cardiac function alterations that occur during T2DM.

title: Enhancing the Interpretability and Applicability of Polygenic Scores through Multi-Omics Integration and Analysis of Family-Based Studies
text:
This proposal aims to create a series of new statistical methods to help us better utilize genetic scores in the
study of the causes behind intricate human diseases. It will incorporate multi-omics data to facilitate molecularly-
informed disease pathways and assess the impact of each pathway on the disease, and also use family-based
studies to provide unbiased investigations of how multiple correlated environmental factors or biomarkers
influence diseases. It will further provide easy-to-use software tools and a summary statistics database for
researchers to analyze large-scale multi-modal data to accelerate future research, enabling a more
comprehensive and unbiased understanding of how molecular changes contribute to human diseases.

title: Determinants of Resistance to Engineered T-cell Therapies Targeting CD19 in Lymphoma
text:
Immune based treatment strategies are increasingly employed to treat patients with Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma
(NHL), but many patients still experience relapse. In this study I seek to identify biomarkers that are predictive
of relapse following immunotherapy, and also to gain an understanding of the mechanisms underlying these
relapses. This project will build a foundation for future clinical trials by informing the development of improved
immunotherapies for this illness, thus directly contributing to the NIH mission to seek basic knowledge about
the nature of living systems that will help to improve health, reduce illness and disability, and lengthen life.

title: Targeting hematopoietic stem cells by lipid nanoparticles to treat hematological disorders
text:
This Program Project Grant will develop safer and more accessible cures for inherited blood disorders, including
sickle cell disease, beta-thalassemia, alpha-thalassemia, and Fanconi anemia. By combining lipid nanoparticles
that directly deliver gene-editing tools to blood stem cells with advanced preclinical models, the program aims to
reduce the toxic side effects of current treatments and make curative therapies available to more patients. These
studies will generate the knowledge and tools needed to advance innovative in vivo and prenatal gene therapy
approaches toward the clinic, ultimately improving survival and quality of life for children and adults living with
these severe conditions.

title: Digital Monitoring of Emotion Regulation and Suicidal Ideation among Individuals at Clinical High Risk for Psychosis
text:
Individuals at clinical high risk for psychosis (CHR-P) are at increased risk for suicide. The proposed study will
combine ecological momentary assessment, wearables, and smartphone-based sensors to examine specific
emotion regulation abnormalities that lead to suicidal ideation among individuals at CHR-P compared to clinical
and non-clinical controls. Identifying the specific emotion regulation abnormalities that lead to suicidal ideation
and novel methods to detect these abnormalities can inform the development of a targeted, scalable suicide
intervention that can be delivered to those who need it most, when they need it most.

title: Next-gen 3D Modeling of Endoscopy Videos
text:
Endoscopies are commonly performed for various diagnostic purposes, and 3D understanding is typically done
in the mind of the clinician performing the procedure and analyzing the endoscopy videos. However current
state-of-the-art techniques for 3D reconstruction use camera motion only and do not work well or fail entirely
for real organs since they lack strong geometric features, have highly reflective mucus layers, and often deform
over time. In this project, we address these challenges by explicitly modeling the reflection of light from mucus
layers and by accounting for time-varying deformation to obtain 3D reconstructions of unprecedented quality.

title: Discovering a multi-protein lipid export system in Mycobacteria
text:
M. tuberculosis remains the leading cause of disease due to an infectious agent worldwide, infecting and killing
millions every year, yet fundamental aspects of its biology are still poorly understood. We do not understand
how M. tuberculosis builds its unique outer membrane, a structure essential for antibiotic resistance and
virulence. Here, we will discover components of MELO (Mycobacterial Exporter of Lipids to the Outer
membrane) and determine their role in lipid transport, uncovering a fundamentally new mechanism in cell
envelope biology with implications for understanding M. tuberculosis pathogenesis.

title: Development and regeneration of retinal ganglion cells in the vertebrate retina
text:
Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by the loss of retinal ganglion cells, affecting over
four million Americans, with a higher prevalence among the elderly. Because the human retina has minimal
regenerative ability, glaucoma can eventually lead to irreversible visual impairment and blindness, with current
therapeutic interventions focused solely on preventing or slowing disease progression. In this grant, we
propose to investigate the transcriptional mechanisms that regulate retinal ganglion cell differentiation during
development, and to apply these insights to formulating strategies for regenerating retinal ganglion cells from
dormant progenitor cells in the adult retina.

title: CSHL Conference on Molecular Mechanisms of Neuronal Connectivity 2026
text:
LAY STATEMENT/Narrative
Molecular Mechanisms of Neuronal Connectivity
September 8 – 11, 2026
The precise wiring, or neuronal connectivity, of the nervous system is the foundation upon which all other
aspects of brain function are based. Neuronal wiring is achieved in a series of discrete and modular
developmental decisions. First, neurons become `polarized', extending dendrites that receive input from
other neurons and a single axon that conveys information to other neurons. Next, `axon guidance'
describes the process by which the axon is guided to the correct target, often extending great distances
through the developing body and brain. Once in the appropriate target region, the axon forms specialized
connections with other neurons, a process that is termed `synapse formation'. Finally, neural circuitry is
refined through the elaboration or elimination of synaptic connections. Understanding these sequential
processes has profound implications for human health. Regeneration of damaged axons and neural circuitry
will require a clear understanding of development. Many neurological diseases are now being clearly
associated with defects in these processes. This conference of approximate 275 scientists will meet to
discuss the latest research in this important field of axon wiring, dendrite formation, synaptogenesis,
regeneration and degeneration of neuronal connections.

title: From Text to Translation: Using Language Models to Resolve and Classify Variants
text:
Deep learning methods toward resolving uncertain variant classifications
Understanding how genetics contributes to disease risk for people in the general population is a major
scientific and medical challenge. The goal of this project is to improve the information that doctors can use
when they care for patients who carry genetic variants which may increase disease risk. We will re-use existing
clinical reports from people who have undergone genetic screenings in order to develop a computational
approach that can help predict whether a genetic variant is likely to cause disease.

title: Understanding the mechanisms by which weight change affects progression of knee osteoarthritis in obese and overweight individuals: An analysis of the Osteoarthritis Initiative Dataset
text:
(Public Health Relevance)
While obesity is a modifiable risk factor for osteoarthritis (OA), studies analyzing the impact of weight loss in
overweight and obese people have found inconsistent results on structural progression of knee OA. One
potential explanation for these findings, and at the same time a major gap of knowledge in previous research, is
that studies have not specifically assessed factors or pathways which, together with mechanical load, are
responsible for improved or worse outcomes, such as associated inflammation, local body composition and
sarcopenia. The overall goal of our proposal is to elucidate which mechanisms are responsible for slowing
progression during weight loss, and which are most beneficial to develop individualized treatment plans targeting
specific pathways that will enhance the positive effects of weight loss on slowing OA progression.

title: DMS/NIGMS 2: Spatial, Multi-Host Petri Net Models for Zoonotic Disease Forecasting
text: This project will construct novel large-scale, multi-host mechanistic models of the Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome (HPS) and Valley Fever (coccidioidomycosis) diseases in the Phoenix, Arizona metro area to investigate the stability versus context-sensitivity of hosts as disease reservoirs and identify key future data sources required to improve forecasting and identify effective interventions aimed at reducing disease burden. Both diseases are endemic to the southwestern United States and are believed to be spread by rodent hosts, but they are caused by different types of pathogens (viruses and fungi, respectively) and show divergent case trends. For training and outreach, the project will implement and evaluate initiatives to (i) communicate results in public outreach events; (ii) construct a course-based undergraduate research experience (CURE) focused on disease modeling; and (iii) build capacity for researching Valley Fever and mitigating outbreaks.

title: Mechanisms and functions of amygdala-hippocampus beta synchrony
text:
We previously identified a pattern of brain activity which tracks self-reported mood and anxiety in human
subjects, then showed that an analogous pattern also influences behavior in mice. Here we will study the
mechanisms and functions of this pattern of activity. We hope this will inform the development of new
strategies for targeting these patterns of activity in order to treat maladaptive avoidance behaviors.

title: Commercialization Readiness for a Portable PET Insert System for Simultaneous TOF-PET and MR Brain Imaging
text:
Neurological and mental health disorders, including Alzheimer's disease, pose a significant financial burden on
the U.S. healthcare system, costing over $800 billion annually. This Commercialization Readiness Pilot program
supports the commercialization of a cost-effective, brain-dedicated, and portable positron emission tomography
(PET) scanner for use as a stand-alone system or with existing MRI systems. The product developed under this
program can make brain PET and combined PET/MRI imaging more widely available, potentially improving early
diagnosis and treatment of neurological and mental health disorders.

title: Genome-wide mutational integration for ultra-sensitive plasma tumor burden monitoring in immunotherapy
text:
The ability to detect low levels of cancer is crucial for cancer diagnosis and treatment; however, even state-of-
the-art techniques such as imaging and ‘liquid biopsy’ through deep sequencing fail to detect cancer when the
tumor burden is extremely low, as can occur after treatment or surgery when small numbers of cancer cells
remain. To address the challenges of detecting such low levels of cancer we propose to make non-incremental
advances in our promising recently developed technology – MRDetect – which uses a sample of the patient's
blood to find low levels of tumor by employing powerful computational tools of artificial intelligence to dramatically
boost cancer detection. We expect that these advances will also foster broad adoption of this new technology
across cancer, empowering precision cancer treatment.

title: Building a spatial transcriptomics infrastructure for isoform profiling in aging pre-neoplastic tissues
text:
Approximately 80% of all breast cancers occur in women older than age 50, but the molecular and cellular
processes that can start the growth of breast tumors during aging are not well known. To help answer this
question, in this project we will build advanced sequencing and visualization tools that will aid researchers in
determining which genes are read to produce which proteins, and where within tissues these events occur. We
will then apply these tools to aging healthy breast tissues as well as breast tumors, which will provide important
information that can be used to develop new approaches for early breast cancer detection, intervention, and
prevention.

title: Uncovering key regulators for the Mitochondrial Ethanol and Stress Response Element and elucidating their role in host defense
text:
This project addresses the urgent public health crisis posed by the proliferation of antimicrobial-resistant
pathogens by uncovering the regulatory mechanisms governing the intersection of mitochondrial surveillance
and innate immunity during pathogenesis. By identifying specific regulators of the Ethanol and Stress Response
Element (ESRE) mitochondrial surveillance pathway and determining their effect on host survival during
pathogenesis, this project advances fundamental knowledge of host defense strategies. Insights from this project
will inform development of novel antimicrobial therapies to harness host immune defenses against pathogens.

title: CRCNS: Computational Mechanisms for State-Driven Active Sensing
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
This research aims to uncover how the brain generates and uses small, fast "active sensing"
movements to enhance behavioral control-mechanisms that are fundamental to everyday actions such
as walking, reaching, and grasping. Conditions like aging, stroke, and diabetes can impair sensory
feedback, disrupting these actions and diminishing quality of life. Based on internal estimates of
uncertainty, we investigate how the nervous system dynamically balances active sensing and goal-directed
control which may reveal new strategies for evaluating and treating movement disorders by
targeting the feedback processes that support motor control.

title: Top-down mechanisms underlying contextual and adaptive processing in the auditory system
text:
Adaptive auditory processing is critical for navigating everyday listening situations that are dynamic and
context-dependent and is known to be compromised in conditions such as aging and hearing loss. The
experiments outlined in this proposal will investigate the circuit and physiological mechanisms underlying
adaptive processing. Therefore, the proposed experiments may identify how adaptive processing is
implemented in normal listening situations and lay the groundwork for investigating how it may be altered in
pathological states.

title: Combatting Multidrug Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii with Chemical Synthetic Lethality
text:
Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, responsible for millions of deaths and immense
economic burden each year. This project will identify novel pairs of drugs to selectively eliminate the antibiotic-
resistant, hospital-acquired pathogen Acinetobacter baumannii by targeting complementary pathways in the cell
using an approach known as chemical synthetic lethality, which is more precise and specific than conventional
therapies. By uncovering these unique drug interactions, the study will provide insights that guide the
development of more effective treatments for difficult-to-treat infections and help reduce the public health impact
of AMR.
